# meshstack_project_tag (Resource)

Manages a single dedicated tag for a meshStack project.

!> **Not recommended for general use.** Prefer managing tags inline via `spec.tags` on `meshstack_project`. Only reach for this resource when the project itself is not managed by your Terraform configuration (for example it was created in meshPanel or by another team) and you understand the trade-offs below. All of them follow from the same limitation: the meshObject API has no endpoint for individual tags, so every create, update and delete here reads the entire `meshProject` object and writes it back with the tags replaced.

~> **The entire project is rewritten on every change.** The Terraform plan only shows a tag changing, but each apply issues a full project update. Everything meshStack does on a project update — audit-log entries, notifications etc. — happens every time, and any project field changed outside Terraform between this resource's read and its write is written back with the value it read.

~> **Tags you do not manage are written back verbatim.** Preserving a project's other tags is what lets several `meshstack_project_tag` resources coexist, but the object read back can carry entries nobody declared here — notably the defaults meshStack injects for restricted tag definitions on a project — and every write sends all of them back. So this resource writes tag entries you never configured, and if your meshStack rejects writing a restricted tag's value, the update fails and no tag on that project can be managed with this resource — use inline `spec.tags` on `meshstack_project` instead. `meshstack_project_tags` is unaffected: it sends exactly the tags you configure.

~> **Race conditions.** The read-modify-write cycle is not atomic and the API offers no optimistic locking. Within a single apply the provider serializes every write to the same project — from this resource, `meshstack_project_tag`, `meshstack_project_tags` and `meshstack_project` alike — so several `meshstack_project_tag` resources on one project keep each other's tags without `depends_on`. Nothing outside that one provider instance is serialized: a concurrent write from another apply, a second provider configuration (alias) pointing at the same meshStack, a panel user, or any other automation can silently clobber this resource's tags or be clobbered by them. Manage all tags of a project from a single Terraform state and never run two applies against the same project in parallel.

~> **Cannot manage tags that are mandatory at project creation.** This resource can only set a tag on a project that already exists, so it cannot supply tag values that meshStack requires when the project is created — the `meshstack_project` create fails before this resource ever runs. Set mandatory tags inline via `spec.tags` on `meshstack_project`.

~> **Subject to change.** This resource is provisional. Once meshStack's meshObject API supports project tags as individual meshObjects, it will be reworked in terms of that API.

~> **The payment methods are written back too.** Every write sends the project's display name, `payment_method_identifier` and `substitute_payment_method_identifier` as it read them. If meshStack switches the project to its substitute payment method between this resource's read and its write, the write puts the old payment method back.

~> **Note:** Do not mix dedicated `meshstack_project_tag` resources with authoritative `meshstack_project_tags` or inline `tags` on `meshstack_project` for the same project. This resource only manages its own key; tags under other keys are read and written back unchanged.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "meshstack_project_tag" "example" {
  metadata = {
    workspace_identifier = data.meshstack_project.example.metadata.owned_by_workspace
    project_identifier   = data.meshstack_project.example.metadata.name
    key                  = data.meshstack_tag_definition.cost_center.spec.key
  }
  spec = {
    values = ["12345"]
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `metadata` (Attributes) Project tag metadata. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metadata))
- `spec` (Attributes) Project tag specification. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec))

<a id="nestedatt--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Required:

- `key` (String) Key of the tag.
- `project_identifier` (String) Identifier of the target project.
- `workspace_identifier` (String) Identifier of the workspace that owns the target project.


<a id="nestedatt--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec`

Required:

- `values` (List of String) List of values for this tag.

## Import

Use the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with an appropriate `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  id = "my-workspace.my-project.cost-center"
  to = meshstack_project_tag.example
}
```

To generate the full resource configuration from the existing remote state, add the `import` block above to your configuration and then run:

```shell
tofu plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
# Terraform equivalent:
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
```

Copy the generated configuration into your root module to start managing the resource with OpenTofu or Terraform.
Note that the generated configuration may require minor adjustments or cleanup, so always run `tofu plan` / `terraform plan` afterwards to verify 
that the configuration fully matches the imported state and that no unintended changes are pending.
If the plan only shows the import of the resource (no other changes), you can run `tofu apply` / `terraform apply` to complete the import. From that point on,
the resource is fully managed via OpenTofu or Terraform.
